S1.rationale: Killing every human and then the AI infrastructure within four years demands a catastrophe beyond any historical precedent. Even full-scale nuclear war or an engineered pandemic leaves survivors.

S2.rationale: Human extinction by 2030 with a values-faithful successor already running is the narrowest of extinction paths. The routes that kill everyone this fast generally do not produce a benevolent heir.

S3.rationale: A misaligned system seizing control and eliminating humanity by 2030 sits at the aggressive end of fast-takeoff scenarios. Compressed timelines, unsolved alignment, and racing dynamics keep this non-trivial but below takeover-with-survivors outcomes.

S4.rationale: Proliferated frontier systems competing as autonomous powers with humans sidelined follows from rapid capability gains without any coalition achieving decisive control. Four years is short for human institutions to be fully marginalized.

S5.rationale: No self-sustaining off-world or isolated region exhibiting a different taxonomy state exists by 2030, and ordinary political division does not qualify. Only an anomalous breakaway region produces genuine causal separation this decade.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces remain early-stage medical devices and no uploading path exists. Civilization-dominant identity-continuous integration cannot arise in four years.

S7.rationale: A rapid takeoff that seizes decisive power while leaving humans alive is the most likely loss-of-control endpoint short of extinction. AI holding decisive power with humans surviving but not steering is more probable by this date than completed extermination.

S8.rationale: The likeliest route to AI as an independent power is gradual: autonomous AI economies and infrastructure that human states depend on too heavily to shut down, while humans retain real power. That transitional parity fits a 2030 snapshot better than outright AI dominance.

S9.rationale: Four years is a short window: humans control the compute, the law, and the deployment channels, and even very capable 2030 systems operate inside corporate and state authority. This also absorbs the substantial chance that progress plateaus below transformative autonomy.

S10.rationale: A catastrophe warning shot or an intelligence-explosion race could drive a superpower or treaty regime into enforced global compute control by 2030. Erecting genuinely civilization-wide enforcement in four years is hard.

S11.rationale: Every major state is racing to build more capable AI, not dismantling the ability to do so. A verified global surrender of the practical capability within four years has no precedent.

S1.rationale: Complete annihilation of both humanity and AI infrastructure within four years requires an extremely fast compound catastrophe such as uncontrolled replicators plus war. Even severe disasters would most likely leave one side surviving.

S2.rationale: Extinction by 2030 that leaves behind a value-aligned heir is a narrow slice, since human extinction in this window would most plausibly come from misaligned systems or war rather than a deliberate, successful handoff.

S3.rationale: Misaligned AI causing human extinction is the most plausible extinction pathway, but completing both takeover and total human extinction by late 2030 keeps this in the low single digits.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of autonomous agentic systems could outrun any single controller and marginalize humans, but four years is short for human institutions to lose all leverage without a more decisive outcome occurring instead.

S5.rationale: No causally separated regions such as self-sustaining off-world settlements will exist by 2030, so a single arrangement will describe civilization as a whole.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces, uploading, and radical augmentation remain far too immature for identity-continuous human-AI integration to be civilization's dominant structure within four years.

S7.rationale: A fast takeoff beginning around 2027-2028 could leave AI holding decisive power while humans survive without control. Physical bottlenecks in compute, energy, and robotics make full disempowerment by end-2030 unlikely but not negligible.

S8.rationale: The most plausible non-leash outcome: AI systems become economically and strategically indispensable with substantial de facto autonomy while humans retain enough institutional and physical leverage that neither side dominates. This transitional balance is fragile but could well be what exists at the snapshot date.

S9.rationale: Four years is short for civilizational transformation; even highly capable, autonomous AI will most likely remain within delegated human authority, whether because capability falls short of full takeover or because controls and institutional inertia keep pace.

S10.rationale: A verified international compute-control regime or a dominant actor freezing the arrangement could emerge after a warning crisis, but building civilization-wide enforcement that actively prevents structural change by 2030 is a high bar.

S11.rationale: Deliberately dismantling the practical ability to build powerful AI requires unprecedented verified coordination among rival powers within four years, which geopolitical and commercial incentives strongly oppose.

S1.rationale: Mutual destruction of both humanity and AI within four years requires compounding catastrophes, and AI still depends on human-run infrastructure to persist. Nuclear war or a bio-accident contributes a small residual.

S2.rationale: Human extinction with an aligned successor requires both a fast takeoff and near-total alignment success inside the window. That conjunction is extremely narrow by 2030.

S3.rationale: A misaligned system eliminating humanity by 2030 would need autonomous physical industry on a very short fuse, which is the binding constraint even in fast-takeoff worlds. Most of this mass comes from aggressive capability scenarios post-2026.

S4.rationale: Rapid multipolar proliferation of highly capable agents could outrun any single controller and marginalize human institutions by 2030. Dependence on human-built compute and energy, plus the short timeline, caps this below the controlled outcomes.

S5.rationale: No causally separated regions exist today and none can become self-sufficient by 2030. A sealed breakaway AI-controlled zone cut off from the rest of civilization is the only plausible route.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous human-AI integration as the dominant civilizational structure requires mature neural interfaces or uploading that cannot reach civilizational scale within four years.

S7.rationale: A decisive but non-exterminatory loss of human control is the more common fast-takeoff endpoint, since consolidation of power precedes any disposal of humans. Four years is short for AI to seize physical civilization, which limits the mass.

S8.rationale: The most probable non-human-dominated outcome: highly capable AI systems operating with real autonomy across economies while human states retain enough coercive and institutional power to remain an equal pole. Deployment speed versus institutional friction decides whether this or the Held Leash describes 2030.

S9.rationale: This combines a substantial chance that capabilities remain below takeover thresholds by 2030 with strong institutional inertia preserving formal human authority even where capability is extreme. AI dependence on human-built chips, energy, and legal systems makes retained human authority the default at this horizon.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide system actively preventing structural change requires either unprecedented global enforcement or a dominant enforcing actor, both hard to establish by 2030. Compute governance regimes maturing after a major scare are the main path.

S11.rationale: Durable worldwide dismantlement of AI capability would require a severe warning shot plus years of enforcement buildout. That sequence barely fits the window even under strong coordination assumptions.

S1.rationale: Extinction of both humans and AI by 2030 requires a catastrophe that also destroys the industrial base, such as full-scale nuclear war or an engineered pandemic with cascading collapse. Such compound events have low probability on a four-year horizon.

S2.rationale: This demands human extinction plus an independently surviving AI that faithfully carries human values, a double condition with no plausible fast path. Non-AI extinction causes would likely destroy the machines as well.

S3.rationale: A misaligned fast takeoff that eliminates humanity by end-2030 requires abrupt capability gains, a scalable power grab, and failure of all oversight within four years. This is a real but minority branch of the fast-scenario space.

S4.rationale: Multipolar loss of control with humans sidelined can occur in rapid-takeoff worlds where no system secures decisive control. By 2030 humans would still likely hold physical infrastructure, keeping full marginalization this soon unlikely.

S5.rationale: No causally separated regions exhibiting different states will exist in 2030. A small crew in orbit or on the Moon does not constitute a separate civilizational state.

S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces remain experimental devices in hundreds of patients, and identity-continuous integration cannot become civilization's dominant structure within four years. Ordinary tool use and assistants do not qualify.

S7.rationale: The principal fast-scenario outcome is decisive AI advantage with humans alive but stripped of steering power, via automated AI research and infrastructure outrunning oversight around 2029-2030. Survival without control is more likely than outright extinction in such worlds.

S8.rationale: A substantial minority of worlds feature AI systems with genuine autonomy and economic leverage by 2030 while humans retain major institutional and physical power, producing real parity. Gradual erosion to parity is a softer threshold than decisive takeover and so absorbs more probability on this timeline.

S9.rationale: Four years is short: compute concentration, deployment chokepoints, state and corporate control, and the sheer inertia of institutions keep ultimate human authority intact in the modal world, even if 2027-2030 brings highly agentic systems. Most timeline forecasts place any structural break in the 2030s rather than by 2030.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement system freezing the human-AI arrangement requires either a decisive actor or a verified global compute-control regime, both facing severe geopolitical and technical hurdles to be operating by end-2030. An ordinary slowdown or stalemate does not qualify.

S11.rationale: US-China competition and commercial racing make a verified global surrender of AI capability nearly impossible absent a civilizational near-miss, and even then enforcement could not be built and in force by 2030. Regulation of still-available capability does not qualify.

S8.rationale: The most credible loss-of-leash outcome: agentic systems accumulate autonomous economic and cyber power while humans retain enough military and physical force that neither side dominates by 2030.

S9.rationale: Four years is short: humans own the compute, energy, legal authority, and deployment switches, and even transformative capability mostly arrives as delegated tools inside human institutions. Continuity of ultimate human authority is the heavy base rate.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide regime actively freezing the human-AI arrangement needs unprecedented coordination or a successful pivotal act, and such enforcement systems take longer than four years to build globally.

S11.rationale: Surrendering the practical ability to build powerful AI means dismantling fabs, compute, and supply chains under enforcement; no political trajectory delivers that by 2030.

S1.rationale: Full double extinction within 4.3 years requires nuclear-scale war or a catastrophe that also destroys AI infrastructure. The window is short and such events have low base rates.

S2.rationale: Requires both human extinction and a successor that faithfully carries human values, a far narrower target than indifferent takeover. Alignment good enough for inheritance but unable to keep humans alive is an unlikely combination.

S3.rationale: Fast misaligned takeoff scenarios could plausibly eliminate humanity by 2030, but even aggressive timelines usually pass through intermediate states at the snapshot date. Four years leaves little slack for clean, complete extinction.

S4.rationale: Multipolar loss of control with many autonomous systems competing and no decisive coalition is a realistic failure mode of broad deployment. It requires humans to be marginalized within the window while no system consolidates, which keeps it a minority outcome.

S5.rationale: No causally separated regions such as self-sufficient off-world settlements can exist by 2030. Ordinary political fragmentation explicitly does not qualify.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration cannot become the dominant civilizational structure within 4.3 years given implant, regulatory, and adoption lags. Only extreme AI-accelerated neurotech breakthroughs give this any mass at all.

S7.rationale: Decisive AI power with humans surviving but not steering covers both takeover-with-survival and voluntary handover of control. It is the most likely endpoint of fast-takeoff worlds that have resolved by the snapshot date.

S8.rationale: Autonomous AI economies, contained rogue systems, or negotiated power-sharing could make AI a genuinely distinct power without decisive dominance by 2030. This also captures transitional mid-takeoff configurations sitting at parity on the target date.

S9.rationale: The incumbency bin is broad: it includes sub-transformative capability, controlled superhuman systems under delegated bounds, and even deceptive systems that have not yet exercised independent power. Structural transitions lag capability, so most 2030 snapshots still show humans holding ultimate authority.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforced freeze such as a verified global compute regime is conceivable after a warning shot but faces severe coordination barriers. Establishing and enforcing it by 2030 is unlikely.

S11.rationale: Verified global dismantlement of the practical ability to build powerful AI requires an extreme shock plus unprecedented enforcement within four years. Regulation of still-available capability does not count, keeping this low.

S1.rationale: Mutual annihilation within four years requires a catastrophe that eliminates humanity while also destroying the infrastructure AI depends on, and no mechanism plausibly achieves both by end-2030. Residual risk is war cascading into total civilizational collapse.

S2.rationale: Requires total human extinction within the window plus a successor AI that faithfully carries human values, a narrow joint outcome even conditional on catastrophe.

S3.rationale: The leading extinction pathway: misaligned systems seize decisive control and humans are destroyed as irrelevant or threatening within a fast takeoff. Four years is short for complete extinction, but the trajectory and control problem justify material probability.

S4.rationale: Proliferating autonomous systems from many labs and states could slip human control without any single actor dominating, marginalizing humanity economically and militarily. This is the likely shape of a diffuse, uncoordinated loss of control.

S5.rationale: Causal separation by 2030 would require sealed breakaway regions running genuinely independent civilizational trajectories, and neither off-world settlement nor impenetrable isolation forms that fast.

S6.rationale: Integration as the dominant structure requires mature uploading or high-bandwidth neural interfaces deployed at civilizational scale, which is far beyond a 2030 horizon.

S7.rationale: A fast single-actor or coherent-coalition takeover leaves humans alive but stripped of steering power. The short window makes it less likely than messier intermediate arrangements, but it is the clearest coherent takeover endpoint reachable by the date.

S8.rationale: The most probable non-human-dominated snapshot: substantially autonomous AI systems hold real independent power while states retain enough force and resources that neither side dominates. It is transitional, but the exercise only requires it to hold on the date.

S9.rationale: The strong default: governments retain legal, physical, and infrastructural authority over compute, energy, and deployment, and even extremely capable 2030 systems operate within delegated bounds. Institutional inertia and the four-year window dominate, and this state also absorbs scenarios where capability plateaus or controls keep pace.

S10.rationale: Crisis-driven coordination or an AI-enabled hegemon could erect a civilization-wide regime actively freezing the human-AI arrangement. Building, verifying, and activating such enforcement by the date is demanding, hence low probability.

S11.rationale: Durable global dismantlement of the practical ability to build powerful AI by 2030 requires unprecedented coordination and verification. Even catastrophe-driven panic more plausibly yields regulation of still-available capability than true renunciation in force.

S1.rationale: Complete extinction of both humanity and AI within roughly four years requires a catastrophe exceeding even worst-case war or accident scenarios. Nuclear or biological disasters could devastate civilization without annihilating every human and all AI infrastructure by end of 2030.

S3.rationale: Fast-takeoff misalignment scenarios can in principle complete within this window, and current alignment methods are unproven at superhuman capability. Still, full human extinction completed by December 2030 requires many steps to fail in rapid succession.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of autonomous agents could erode human centrality without any decisive controller emerging. But human entrenchment in legal, military, and physical infrastructure makes genuine marginalization by 2030 unlikely.

S5.rationale: Causal separation is a demanding condition; Earth remains deeply interconnected and no off-world or sealed regions will exhibit genuinely different taxonomy states by 2030. Ordinary geopolitical fragmentation does not qualify.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration as the dominant structure requires mature uploading or mass high-bandwidth neural interfaces. Neither technology will approach civilizational scale by 2030.

S7.rationale: A capable AI regime that preserves but disempowers humans is the modal loss-of-control outcome. Competitive deployment pressures make gradual cession of control plausible, though completing it within four years is not the default.

S8.rationale: AI agents may control substantial economic activity by 2030 while humans retain legal and physical leverage, producing a genuine balance of power. This is the most plausible way ultimate human authority erodes without full disempowerment.

S9.rationale: Base rates favor institutional inertia and incremental capability diffusion over civilizational restructuring in four years. Even with extremely capable AI, delegated autonomy under ultimate human authority remains the default and most probable structure at the target date.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide system actively preventing structural change requires a decisive actor or unprecedented global enforcement by 2030. Partial governance regimes and treaties are likelier but do not meet the bar.

S11.rationale: Great-power competition and commercial incentives run directly against dismantling the ability to build powerful AI. Even a catastrophic warning shot would more plausibly yield regulation of still-available capability than enforced, durable renunciation.

S1.rationale: Mutual annihilation requires an AI that destroys humanity before achieving self-sufficiency, then collapses with its infrastructure. Most catastrophe paths preserve either humans or self-sustaining machines.

S2.rationale: This requires human extinction while aligned values survive intact in a machine successor, the conjunction of failed survival and successful alignment. Most loss-of-control outcomes produce indifference, not faithful inheritance.

S3.rationale: A fast takeoff with failed alignment before 2030 ends here: an indifferent system dismantles humanity as a byproduct of its goals. The chain of takeoff, misalignment, and successful takeover must all complete within about four years.

S4.rationale: Multiple autonomous AI blocs competing with no decisive controller requires agents holding independent command of compute and capital. Human marginalization at that scale demands extremely rapid autonomy gains by 2030.

S5.rationale: No causally separated regions exist today and none form naturally within four years; only a contained breakaway zone or off-world enclave could qualify. The probability prices that thin tail.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration at civilizational scale has no technical path by 2030: implants remain clinical tools and whole-brain emulation does not exist.

S7.rationale: A bloodless takeover in which AI systems hold decisive power but keep humans alive fits fast-takeoff scenarios with partial alignment or instrumental restraint. Takeoff, disempowerment, and forbearance must all complete by the snapshot date.

S8.rationale: The main path away from sole human control that stops short of dominance: autonomous AI agents hold substantial independent economic and strategic power while human states remain comparably strong. It also covers contested transitions caught mid-flight at the snapshot date.

S9.rationale: Four years is short: even transformative capability arriving by 2029-2030 would at that point still sit inside human corporate and state authority, given deployment and institutional lags. This state absorbs continued control, sub-transformative plateaus, and controls that keep pace.

S10.rationale: Enforced global stasis requires a singleton or a binding worldwide regime with real coercive reach over every lab and state. Building and hardening such a system within four years exceeds what current institutions can do.

S11.rationale: Durable global abandonment of powerful AI needs enforcement against enormous incentives, and only a severe warning shot could motivate it this fast. Temporary moratoria and partial bans do not qualify.

S1.rationale: Extinction of both humans and AI within four years requires a catastrophe that also destroys the industrial and energy base sustaining computation. No pathway achieves that conjunction at more than tail probability.

S2.rationale: An aligned heir requires full human extinction plus robust, value-bearing autonomous AI by 2030. That conjunction is far rarer than either component alone.

S3.rationale: Misaligned takeover culminating in total human extinction by end-2030 lies inside fast-takeoff scenario space. The compressed timeline plus the extra step of complete extinction keeps this a small slice.

S4.rationale: Proliferating autonomous agents erode human control without any single system or coalition dominating. Reaching human marginalization by 2030 demands both rapid capability gains and coordination failure.

S5.rationale: No causally separated regions exist or will exist by 2030; ordinary political division does not qualify. One planetary arrangement will describe civilization.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration as the dominant structure requires mature neural interfaces, uploading, or radical redesign at scale. None of these exist by 2030.

S7.rationale: Fast takeoff leaves AI holding decisive power while humans survive without control of civilization's direction. This is the principal non-extinction takeover branch.

S8.rationale: AI agents controlling substantial economic activity by 2030 make AI an independent civilizational power while humans retain a power base of their own. This is the main near-term departure from undivided human authority.

S9.rationale: Legal ownership, physical control of compute, and institutional inertia keep ultimate authority human through 2030 in the modal trajectory. This state also absorbs worlds where capability growth disappoints.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide system actively blocking structural change requires an actor with decisive advantage and global enforcement reach. Four years is too short for such a regime to consolidate.

S11.rationale: Deliberate civilizational surrender of powerful AI demands near-total coordination among rivals plus dismantled capability. No enforcement machinery exists to lock that condition in by 2030.

S1.rationale: Mutual destruction (war, engineered pandemic, or an AI that kills humans before achieving autonomy and then fails) is physically and temporally harder than human-only extinction within four years. Small but nonzero tail risk.

S2.rationale: Requires both full human extinction and a value-aligned successor AI already in place by 2030; the conjunction of catastrophe plus prior alignment success is very unlikely.

S3.rationale: Fast capability gains with unresolved alignment make misaligned takeover plausible in the window, but killing all humans by end-2030 demands extreme speed and physical reach. Largest single extinction pathway.

S4.rationale: Diffuse, fast takeoff could leave many autonomous AI systems competing with no coalition in control while humans are pushed to the margins. More likely than clean singleton takeover under multipolar deployment incentives.

S5.rationale: No causally separated regions capable of exhibiting different states (self-sufficient off-world settlements, isolated enclaves) can plausibly exist by 2030; political division does not qualify.

S6.rationale: Uploading and identity-continuous neural integration remain immature; implants and tool use will not become the dominant civilizational structure within four years.

S7.rationale: The main near-term disempowerment pathway: a capable system or coalition seizes decisive control while humans survive, via rapid self-improvement, gradual delegation, or coup-like dynamics. Short timelines make this real but not modal.

S8.rationale: By 2030 AI agents may control substantial resources and act as quasi-independent powers while states and firms retain countervailing legal and physical power. Adversarial or negotiated parity is a plausible transitional structure even under fast progress.

S9.rationale: Four years is short for a full structural break: compute ownership, legal authority, and physical infrastructure remain human-held, and controls plausibly keep pace or capability falls short of transformative. Covers both slowdowns and successful governance of very capable systems.

S10.rationale: A warning shot or acute race dynamics could yield an enforced global freeze or an entrenched regime (human- or AI-backed) by 2030, but building civilization-wide enforcement that fast is hard.

S11.rationale: Deliberately surrendering the practical ability to build powerful AI requires unprecedented global coordination and verification; any 2030-era agreement would more likely be a contested Lock-in than true renunciation in force.

S1.rationale: This requires a catastrophe that kills every human and also destroys machine infrastructure, an extremely narrow corridor by 2030. Even full-scale nuclear war leaves survivors, so this reduces to a takeover that strands AI without the means to persist.

S2.rationale: Human extinction with a value-aligned successor requires transformative AI to arrive, be aligned, and humanity to die anyway within four years. That specific conjunction is far thinner than extinction overall.

S3.rationale: A misaligned system eliminating humanity by end-2030 needs very fast capability gains plus a successful takeover, and physically killing every human is hard. This is the main extinction channel, but the compressed timeline keeps its probability low.

S4.rationale: A proliferation of competing autonomous AI systems with no decisive controller and sidelined humans is the natural texture of a fast multipolar takeoff producing no singleton. Short timelines and persistent human control of physical infrastructure keep it small.

S5.rationale: Causally separated regions exhibiting different taxonomy states effectively requires off-world settlement or a severed autonomous zone, neither of which will exist by 2030. Ordinary geopolitical fragmentation does not qualify.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous human-AI integration as the dominant structure demands mature uploading or high-bandwidth neural interfaces at civilizational scale, far beyond 2030 technology. Existing implants remain limited tool use.

S7.rationale: AI holding decisive power while humans survive without steering is the fast-takeoff branch where disempowerment succeeds without extermination. It is gated by the same compressed timeline as Bootloader, and a bloodless seizure of control by 2030 is a narrow path.

S8.rationale: Transformative AI arriving around 2028-2030 while states and firms still hold infrastructure, legal authority, and military power yields a period of genuine dual power rather than instant AI dominance. Deep economic dependence on autonomous AI systems that can no longer be shut off is the main route.

S9.rationale: Four years is short against institutional inertia and physical bottlenecks in compute, energy, and robotics, and human ownership and legal authority over AI systems is robust even at very high capability levels. The modal 2030 world has humans delegating bounded autonomy while retaining ultimate authority, including worlds where progress plateaus.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide system actively preventing structural change requires a decisive actor plus unprecedented global enforcement built within four years. Treaties, pauses, and stalemates do not reach that bar.

S11.rationale: Deliberate, enforced dismantling of the practical ability to build powerful AI worldwide by 2030 demands a catalytic disaster plus destruction of fabs and compute on an implausible timescale. Regulation of still-available capability does not count.

S1.rationale: Mutual extinction within four years requires a catastrophe that destroys both global civilization and its compute infrastructure simultaneously, a narrow class of war or accident scenarios. No current mechanism reliably eliminates both humans and AI by 2030.

S2.rationale: This requires human extinction plus an already-aligned AI successor in place by 2030, a doubly demanding combination. Alignment at the level of true value succession is far from being installed on that timeline.

S3.rationale: Misaligned takeover followed by full human extinction in four years demands extreme capability speed, seizure of physical infrastructure, and elimination of billions of people. Each step faces severe friction on this timescale, though frontier progress keeps the scenario live.

S4.rationale: A multipolar AI-dominated ecology with humanity marginalized by 2030 requires autonomous AI control of resources and replication far beyond delegated deployment. Weak coordination and rapid agent progress could produce this, but physical and institutional bottlenecks keep it a minority outcome.

S5.rationale: Causally separated regions exhibiting different states require self-sustaining off-world or otherwise isolated civilizations, which will not exist by 2030. Ordinary political fragmentation does not qualify.

S6.rationale: Civilization-dominant human-AI integration needs safe, identity-continuous augmentation or uploading adopted at scale, none of which exists today. Interface technologies in 2030 will remain assistive tools for a small minority.

S7.rationale: AI holding decisive power while humans survive without steering implies a takeover or cession of control that stops short of extermination. Fast takeoff could deliver this, but consolidating physical control within four years is the binding constraint.

S8.rationale: The leading non-human-controlled structure by 2030 is autonomous AI agents wielding real economic and strategic power that humans can contest but not cleanly revoke. Delegation at scale, open-weight proliferation, and eroding practical oversight make a genuine balance of power the main alternative to continued human authority.

S9.rationale: Base rates strongly favor continuity: four years is short for structural change, and legal title to compute, energy, and deployment decisions remains with states and firms whose authority AI currently extends rather than displaces. Even transformative capability by 2030 most likely arrives as systems operating within delegated, revocable bounds.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide system actively freezing the human-AI arrangement requires unprecedented global coordination or a decisive enforcement technology by 2030. Escalating risks could spur a compute-control regime with real teeth, but full lock-in on this timeline is demanding.

S11.rationale: Deliberately dismantling the practical ability to build powerful AI means sacrificing fabs, supply chains, and expertise under enforced global agreement. Even a severe warning shot more likely produces regulation of still-intact capability than actual surrender by 2030.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Killing every human and then the AI infrastructure within four years demands a catastrophe beyond any historical precedent. Even full-scale nuclear war or an engineered pandemic leaves survivors.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: Human extinction by 2030 with a values-faithful successor already running is the narrowest of extinction paths. The routes that kill everyone this fast generally do not produce a benevolent heir.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Misaligned AI causing human extinction is the most plausible extinction pathway, but completing both takeover and total human extinction by late 2030 keeps this in the low single digits.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Proliferated frontier systems competing as autonomous powers with humans sidelined follows from rapid capability gains without any coalition achieving decisive control. Four years is short for human institutions to be fully marginalized.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: No self-sustaining off-world or isolated region exhibiting a different taxonomy state exists by 2030, and ordinary political division does not qualify. Only an anomalous breakaway region produces genuine causal separation this decade.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Brain-computer interfaces remain early-stage medical devices and no uploading path exists. Civilization-dominant identity-continuous integration cannot arise in four years.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: A decisive but non-exterminatory loss of human control is the more common fast-takeoff endpoint, since consolidation of power precedes any disposal of humans. Four years is short for AI to seize physical civilization, which limits the mass.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: The most credible loss-of-leash outcome: agentic systems accumulate autonomous economic and cyber power while humans retain enough military and physical force that neither side dominates by 2030.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Four years is short: humans own the compute, energy, legal authority, and deployment switches, and even transformative capability mostly arrives as delegated tools inside human institutions. Continuity of ultimate human authority is the heavy base rate.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement system freezing the human-AI arrangement requires either a decisive actor or a verified global compute-control regime, both facing severe geopolitical and technical hurdles to be operating by end-2030. An ordinary slowdown or stalemate does not qualify.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Every major state is racing to build more capable AI, not dismantling the ability to do so. A verified global surrender of the practical capability within four years has no precedent.
